Your life can look completely different in the next 40 days, but only if you stop repeating the habits that keep you stuck.

How many times have you promised yourself that tomorrow would be different? Then tomorrow comes, and the same routine begins again.

The truth is, your future is shaped by the little things you do every day.

Start by cleaning your space and identifying the habits that hold you back. Build a routine you can actually follow. You donât have to change your life overnight. Choose a consistent wake-up time, take care of your body, and make time for the goals that matter.

Give yourself 30 days to focus on personal growth. Learn a new skill, read, exercise, or work on something that could improve your future. Small actions may not feel powerful today, but repeated consistently, they can change your direction.

Stop waiting until you feel ready. Confidence grows when you keep promises to yourself. Discipline develops when you do what matters, even when you donât feel like doing it.

You will have difficult days. You might fall back into an old habit. That doesnât mean youâve failed. Youâre human. Just donât let one bad day become another bad month.

Keep track of your small wins. Notice what youâre learning and what youâre improving. On days when you doubt yourself, look back and see how far youâve come.

Stop comparing your progress to someone elseâs life. You donât know their struggles or starting point. Your real competition is the version of you that keeps making excuses.

Imagine where you could be 40 days from now if you spent less time overthinking and more time taking action. You donât need to become a different person overnight. Just make choices that bring you closer to who you want to be.

For a receiver it is a completely different question. Only 22% of passing scores come from inside the 5, and about a third start outside the red zone entirely. For him it is volume and explosiveness, not field position.

So red zone usage is close to the whole story for one group and under half of it for the other.

Almost everybody runs one method across both. That is the error.

Store salsa sits in a jar on a shelf for a year. Think about that. Nothing with living cultures in it can last that long. It's cooked, pasteurized, and shelf-stable, which is a nice way of saying dead.

Tomatoes, onion, jalapeÃ±o, garlic, cilantro, minced together. Then salt at about 2%, a squeeze of lemon, a stir, and it sits on the counter for a few days.

Same salsa everyone loves. Except this one's working for you, and it keeps for months.

deli meats contain several ingredients that are bad for your health, including nitrates and nitrites, phosphates, processed additives + chemical contaminants

but donât be fooled by meat labeled as ânitrate freeâ. these meats use natural sources of nitrates, but they can still convert into nitrosamines in the body

so next time youâre craving a deli sandwich, try making your own deli meat with 3 simple ingredients instead

YOU NEED

Cops have access to tools that have scraped billions of images from the web, letting them identify essentially anyone by pointing a phone camera at them. Being aware of all the ways your face is being recognized by algorithms and sometimes collected by cameras when you walk outside can start to feel overwhelming at best, and futile to resist at worst. But there are ways to disguise yourself from facial recognition systems in your everyday life.

In the years since the Dazzle project made adversarial design mainstream, there have been lots of projects that attempt to confound, pollute, or elude the cameras that watch us move through the world every day. Adam Harvey has made several more, including heat obscuring ponchos meant to hide the wearer from drones, Faraday cage pockets for phones, and high-powered LED flash arrays for blinding paparazzi. But much of the wearables in this genreâfrom high-fashion streetwear shops to cheap listings by dropshippersârely on 2D printed designs that donât keep up with how quickly algorithms change and improve. The $600 hoodie with a cool pixel design on it might have worked yesterday, in perfect conditions, but the next time the cameras in the mall update their algorithms or datasets, it doesnât work anymore.

All of this sounds complex and sophisticated, but these systems arenât necessarily hard to fool. It turns out, you probably already own the most effective anti-surveillance fashion: a cloth mask. @evystadium breaks it down.

Cozy, comforting and easy! This tuna melt is fish free and delicious ð¤¤ Hollander approved ð 

Makes 3 sandwiches.

Ingredients:
1 can chickpeas, drained and mashed 
1/2 red onion, finely diced
1 dill pickle, finely diced
2 tbsp capers + 1 tbsp brine
1 tbsp white miso paste
1 tsp salt + 1tbsp crushed nori
1/2 cup mayo
3 slices of vegan cheddar
6 slices of bread

Method:
1. In a large bowl, add the chickpeas and mash with a potato masher until all the chickpeas are mashed up and it resembles the texture of tuna. 2. Turn your oven to a low broil and broil both slices of bread until golden. Flip the bread and place one piece on a baking sheet. So you "deleted" your sensitive files and emptied the Trash/Recycle Bin. Congratulations. You've done the digital equivalent of tearing the address page out of a phone book. The data is still there, sitting idle, waiting for the next cheap recovery tool to bring it all back to life. It's not a matter of "if," but "when."

ð The Grim Reality of "Delete":

Â· It just removes the file system's pointer.
Â· The actual 1s and 0s remain on the drive platters or memory chips.
Â· With basic software, anyone can resurrect contracts, financial records, client databases, and personal photos.

ð¡ï¸ THE ACTUAL SOLUTION: DoD 5220.22-M (NISPOM)
We don't "delete." We obliterate.
This isn't just some fancy term. It's the U.S. Department of Defense's gold standard for sanitizing classified information from magnetic media.

Hereâs what our 3-pass overwrite actually does:

1. Pass 1: Overwrites all addressable locations with a binary zero (0x00).
2. Pass 2: Overwrites all locations with a binary one (0xFF).
3. Pass 3: Overwrites all locations with a cryptographically secure random bit pattern.
4. THE CRITICAL STEP: A final verification pass reads all sectors to confirm the overwrite was successful.

Ham + Cheese Hot Pockets
INGREDIENTS

Dough
-4 cups (500g) AP flour
-2 teaspoons (10g) kosherfine salt
-1 tablespoon (12g) sugar
-1 packet (7g) yeast (active dry or instant I donât know the difference)
-1 1/4 cups (300g) warm water
-2 tablespoons (30g) olive oil or melted butter

Filling
-8 ounces deli ham
-8 ounces mild cheddar, shredded

Topping
-2 ounces salted butter, melted
-Flaky salt
-Poppy seeds, optional

Dough Instructions
1. Combine dry ingredients: flour, salt, sugar, and yeast.
2. Add warm water + oil. Mix until it becomes a rough dough.
3. Knead (8 minutes) or stand mix (5 minutes) until smooth.
4. Cover 1 to 1.5 hours until dough rises and doubles in size..
5. Divide into 12 balls. Rest 10 minutes before filling.

Filling + Bake
1. Flatten or roll each dough ball to about 4â across.
2. Add ham + cheddar. Close + pinch to seal; place seam-side down.
3. Cut tiny slits to vent. Brush w/ butter, salt ,and poppy seeds.
4. Bake at 425Â°F for 15-18 min until golden.
